CHAPTER 01 Naming Conventions Master Reference Names are the cheapest documentation you will ever write. This chapter is the lookup table for Java and Spring. CHAPTER 03 Self-Explanatory Code Good names let a reader skip the implementation. Four habits get you there. Name by intent ✗ VAG U E processData() , handleRequest() INTENT-REVEALING calculateMonthlyInterest(), validatePaymentRequest() ✗ VAG U E temp , x INTENT-REVEALING retryAttemptCount , customerId ✗ VAG U E flag , value INTENT-REVEALING isPaymentEligible , remainingQuota Method prefixes carry a contract Retrieval verbs, ordered by cost, cheap to expensive: get in-memory read → find lookup, may be absent → load storage to memory → fetch remote call, latency get Cheap, side-effect-free access to existing state getStatus() find Lookup that may return nothing ( Optional or empty collection) findDeviceById(id) fetch Remote or expensive retrieval (HTTP, SSH, DB join) fetchRunningConfig(device) load Read from storage into memory, or initialise a resource loadRetryPolicies() calculate Pure derivation of a value calculateMonthlyInterest(loan) validate Check rules; throws or returns a result, never silently mutates validatePaymentRequest(req) create / of / from Factories: create makes new; of and from are static factories Money.of(100, INR) build Assemble a complex object step by step buildBackupCommand(device) convert / to / map Change representation: to returns another type, map maps models toResponse() , mapToEntity(dto) is / has / can Boolean question with no side effects hasExpired() , canRetry() handle / on Event or message entry points (listeners, handlers) onDeviceOffline(event) process Only for a real pipeline with defined stages; else name the work processBackupQueue() action verbs Commands: verb + domain noun scheduleBackup() , cancelJob(id)

Skip meaningless prefixes ( doX , performX , manageX ) and words already implied by the type or class. Class names communicate responsibility ✗ RESPONSIBILITY UNCLEAR DataManager , CommonUtil , Helper , Processor RESPONSIBILITY OBVIOUS PaymentValidator , InvoiceGenerator , DeviceBackupScheduler Avoid misleading names ✗ SMELL Unclear abbreviation B A D cfgMgr , bkpSt BETTER configManager , backupStatus W H Y Saves keystrokes, costs minutes ✗ SMELL Wrong boolean B A D boolean status , notDisabled BETTER isEnabled W H Y Read as true/false; avoid negations ✗ SMELL Hidden side effect B A D getConnection() that opens one BETTER openConnection() W H Y get promises a cheap read ✗ SMELL Too generic B A D Map data , process(Object o) BETTER Map statusByDevice W H Y Name the key-to-value meaning ✗ SMELL Too long B A D getAllDevicesThatNeedBackupNow() findDevicesDueForBackup() BETTER W H Y Express the concept, not the query ✗ SMELL Redundant B A D device.getDeviceName() device.getName() BETTER W H Y Context already supplies the noun Remember. A prefix is a promise. If get ever opens a connection, the name is lying.

CHAPTER 04 Extract Methods, Classes and Responsibilities Extraction is how you give a block of logic a name. Do it when the name earns its place. Decision guide Ask these in order. Does the block have a meaningful, independent purpose? Yes: extract a method , and give the block a name. Is it a distinct responsibility or business concept? Yes: extract a class , and let it own the concept. Otherwise keep the implementation simple. Design principles behind the guide: one reason to change per class; keep HTTP, rules and persistence apart; members of a class belong together; depend on small interfaces and inject them; inherit only for a true "is-a".

Extract a method when… It performs several logically distinct steps. A block has a meaningful, independent purpose. The same logic is duplicated. You must scroll or re-read to follow it. Nested conditions hide the main path. A section deserves a descriptive name. Create a separate class when… It mixes unrelated responsibilities. Parts change for different business reasons. A dependency serves only one separate concern. The logic needs independent testing or reuse. A business concept deserves its own abstraction. The class is hard to understand or maintain.

Extract method: before One block, four concerns. public void backup(Device d) { if (d != null && d.getStatus() == DeviceStatus.ONLINE && d.getIp() != null) { String cfg = ssh.run(d.getIp(), "show running-config"); if (cfg != null && !cfg.isBlank()) { repo.save(new Backup(d.getId(), cfg, Instant.now())); log.info("Backup done for {}", d.getId()); } } } Extract method: after Reads like the requirement. public void backup(Device device) { if (!isBackupEligible(device)) return; String config = fetchRunningConfig(device); if (config.isBlank()) return; saveBackup(device, config); } private boolean isBackupEligible(Device d) { return d != null && d.getStatus() == DeviceStatus.ONLINE && d.getIp() != null; }

Extract class: split by reason to change Before: one OrderService with four reasons to change. OrderService validate(order) // business rules calculatePrice(order) // pricing policy save(order) // persistence sendConfirmation() // email channel After: OrderService orchestrates the use case and delegates to cohesive collaborators: business rules, pricing policy, persistence, email channel. When not to extract Not every 3-line block needs a method. Extract when it earns a name, not to hit a length target. Not every field deserves its own class. Avoid abstractions with a single, speculative use. Don't create classes just to follow a pattern, or one-method wrappers with no real responsibility. Remember. Extract to reveal intent, not to hit a number.

CHAPTER 05 Comments, Constants and the Final Checklist Comments explain why, never what Noise: // increment counter counter++; // get user by id User getUserById(long id) { ... } // old logic // if (retry > 5) return; Adds knowledge the code can't: // Gateway rejects payloads above 1 MB, // so split first List chunks = splitByMaxSize(config); // Overdue 5 days after due date (contract §4.2) return today.isAfter(dueDate.plusDays(5)); // TODO(BKP-214): drop after v2 API migration Explaining why: trade-off, workaround, constraint It repeats the method name or signature

Recording a non-obvious business rule It narrates an obvious statement Documenting a complex algorithm or invariant It is commented-out code (version control remembers) Javadoc on public APIs and shared modules It is outdated: delete or fix it TODO / FIXME with a ticket and owner Excessive inline commentary; rename or extract instead Magic numbers and hardcoded values Bad: if (retryCount > 3) { // retry } Better: private static final int MAX_RETRY_COUNT = 3; if (retryCount > MAX_RETRY_COUNT) { // retry } Fixed, code-owned A named constant MAX_RETRY_COUNT = 3

A closed set of states An enum (with behaviour if needed) BackupStatus.IN_PROGRESS Tunable per environment A configuration property, bound to a typed class backup.retry.max-attempts Secret or endpoint External config: env var, Kubernetes Secret / ConfigMap ${DB_PASSWORD} Spring Boot: typed configuration @ConfigurationProperties(prefix = "backup.retry") public record RetryProperties( int maxAttempts, Duration backoff) {} # application.yml backup: retry: max-attempts: 3 backoff: 2s Not every literal needs a constant. 0 , 1 , "" , list.get(0) or total / 2 are self-evident. A constant like ZERO = 0 adds indirection, not meaning. Name a value when its reason isn't obvious.

Final clean-code checklist Does the class name describe its responsibility? Does the method name explain its intent? Are variable names meaningful? Are boolean names expressed as questions? Are abbreviations understandable? Are naming conventions consistent? Are methods focused on one logical task? Does each class have a cohesive responsibility? Are magic numbers avoided where appropriate? Do comments explain why rather than what? Are configuration values externalised appropriately? Are duplication and unnecessary abstractions avoided? Can another developer understand it without asking its author? The one principle to remember. Write code for the developer who will maintain it six months from now, not just for the compiler that executes it today.

CHAPTER 06 YAML, JSON and API Naming Golden rule: the tool that reads the file decides the style. Where the format is yours (your config keys, your API), pick one convention and never mix. STD means fixed by a spec or framework; TEAM means our choice, agree once. YAML files: which key style where application.yml K E Y S kebab-case EXAMPLE retry-max-attempts: 3 N OT E S STD Spring recommends it Env var override K E Y S UPPER_SNAKE EXAMPLE ORDERSERVICE_RETRY_MAXATTEMPTS N OT E S STD dashes dropped, dots become _ Helm values.yaml K E Y S camelCase EXAMPLE replicaCount: 2 N OT E S STD flat over nested; quote strings Kubernetes manifest K E Y S camelCase EXAMPLE imagePullPolicy: IfNotPresent N OT E S STD API fields; names stay kebab-case GitHub Actions K E Y S fixed keys EXAMPLE runs-on , timeout-minutes N OT E S STD job ids: kebab-case Docker Compose K E Y S snake_case EXAMPLE depends_on , container_name N OT E S STD service names: kebab-case

OpenAPI spec K E Y S camelCase EXAMPLE operationId: cancelOrder N OT E S STD schemas: PascalCase Spring Boot application.yml Grouped by prefix, kebab-case, units on values: order-service: retry: max-attempts: 3 backoff-delay: 500ms kafka: topics: order-confirmed: orders.confirmed spring: datasource: password: ${DB_PASSWORD} It binds to a typed properties class: @ConfigurationProperties(prefix = "order-service") public record OrderServiceProperties(Retry retry) { public record Retry(int maxAttempts, Duration backoffDelay) {} }

Avoid: OrderService: Retry_MaxAttempts: 3 backoffMS: 500 db_pwd: s3cret enableNotifications: false Prefix is kebab-case; Java fields stay camelCase, and Spring maps them. Use positive boolean names: enabled: true , not disabled: false . Put units on values ( 500ms , 30s ), not in key names. Secrets are placeholders: ${DB_PASSWORD} , never literals. Quote look-alikes: country: "NO" (YAML 1.1 reads bare NO as false). Use 2-space indent, no tabs, no duplicate keys. JSON files that are not API payloads Config / data feature-flags.json kebab-case file names; camelCase keys TEAM JSON Schema order-confirmed.v1.schema.json Version in the name; $schema and $id are required spec keywords STD

Test fixtures order-created.json Under src/test/resources/fixtures/ ; named after the scenario Tool files package.json Names fixed by the tool; never rename STD JSON has no comments. If a config file needs explanations, use YAML instead. One setting, four spellings Same meaning, each tool's own case. application.yml retry.max-attempts → env variable RETRY_MAXATTEMPTS → Java field maxAttempts → Helm value retryMaxAttempts Spring's relaxed binding maps the first three automatically. Helm keys are yours: translate them into env vars in the Deployment template, in one place only.

Request and response JSON Pick one case for the whole API. camelCase matches Jackson and Java records out of the box. For snake_case, set spring.jackson.property-naming- strategy: SNAKE_CASE once, globally. Never mix both in one API. POST /api/v1/orders request: { "customerId": "c-1042", "items": [ { "sku": "KB-001", "quantity": 2 } ], "shippingAddress": { "postalCode": "560001", "country": "IN" } } 201 Created response: { "id": "9f1c2e7a-…", "status": "PAYMENT_PENDING", "total": { "amount": "49.90", "currency": "INR" }, "emailVerified": true, "createdAt": "2026-11-09T10:15:30Z" } ✗ CONCERN Field names RULE Singular nouns; plural for collections GOOD / BAD customerId , items vs Customer_ID ✗ CONCERN Booleans RULE Plain adjective; Jackson drops is from isX() getters GOOD / BAD active , emailVerified ✗ CONCERN Timestamps RULE ISO 8601 / RFC 3339, UTC, suffix At TEAM GOOD / BAD createdAt vs created: 1731147330 ✗ CONCERN Money RULE Decimal string plus ISO 4217 currency; never a float TEAM GOOD / BAD "49.90" + "INR" ✗ CONCERN Enum values RULE UPPER_SNAKE, same as the Java enum TEAM GOOD / BAD PAYMENT_PENDING

✗ CONCERN Nulls RULE Omit empty fields: spring.jackson.default-property- inclusion: non_null GOOD / BAD not "middleName": null ✗ CONCERN IDs RULE Own id is id ; references are xxxId ; strings, not numbers GOOD / BAD id , customerId Error responses: RFC 9457 Problem Details 409 , content type application/problem+json : { "type": "https://api.example.com/problems/duplicate", "title": "Duplicate order", "status": 409, "detail": "Idempotency key already used.", "instance": "/api/v1/orders", "traceId": "4bf92f35…", "errors": [ { "field": "items[0].sku", "message": "unknown" } ] } Five standard members: type , title , status , detail , instance .

Extensions ( traceId , errors ) use the same case as the API TEAM . In Spring, return ProblemDetail , or set spring.mvc.problemdetails.enabled: true for built- in exceptions. One error shape for every service. Never leak stack traces. URLs, parameters, headers, status codes Resource path Plural nouns, kebab-case, version prefix TEAM /api/v1/order-items Path variable camelCase, matches the JSON field /orders/{orderId} Query params camelCase; filter by field name TEAM ?status=SHIPPED&customerId=c-1042 Pagination Spring Data defaults: page , size , sort=prop,dir ?page=0&size=20&sort=createdAt,desc Headers Hyphenated Title-Case; avoid new X- prefixes (RFC 6648) Idempotency-Key , Correlation-Id

Status codes 201 + Location , 400 , 404 , 409 , 422 create, bad input, missing, conflict, invalid Kafka event payloads follow the same rules orders.confirmed , envelope plus payload: { "eventId": "b7e2…", "eventType": "order.confirmed", "eventVersion": 1, "occurredAt": "2026-11-09T10:15:30Z", "payload": { "orderId": "9f1c2e7a-…", "total": { "amount": "49.90", "currency": "INR" } } } Remember. Events are contracts too: add fields freely, never rename or remove them without bumping eventVersion .

CHAPTER 07 Git Naming and Versioning Four namespaces, four jobs Commit What kind of change is this? Lives in Git history and drives the changelog feat(order): add retry Issue / PR labels How do we triage this? Lives on issues and pull requests type: bug , priority: high Branch Where is this work happening? Temporary; deleted after merge feature/PAY-142-kafka-retry Tag What exactly did we ship? Permanent pointer to a release commit v1.5.0

Branch feature/PAY-142-… → Commits feat(scope): … → Pull request title + labels → Main squash merge → Tag v1.5.0 Conventional commit types feat and fix are defined by the Conventional Commits spec. The other core types follow the Angular convention used by commitlint. TEAM types are custom and you must configure them yourself. feat USE IT FOR New capability or API EXAMPLE feat(order-service): add order cancellation endpoint RELEASE MINOR fix USE IT FOR Bug fix EXAMPLE fix(device-backup): retry SSH on connection timeout RELEASE PATCH docs USE IT FOR Documentation only EXAMPLE docs(api): document 409 for duplicate payments RELEASE none style USE IT FOR Formatting, no behaviour change EXAMPLE style: apply google-java-format RELEASE none refactor USE IT FOR Restructure, same behaviour EXAMPLE refactor(order): extract PricingCalculator RELEASE none perf USE IT FOR Performance improvement EXAMPLE perf(catalog): cache product lookups in Redis RELEASE PATCH test USE IT FOR Add or fix tests EXAMPLE test(payment): add Testcontainers Kafka IT RELEASE none build USE IT FOR Build system, dependencies EXAMPLE build(deps): bump spring-boot to 3.4.0 RELEASE none ci USE IT FOR CI/CD pipeline EXAMPLE ci: cache Maven repository in GitHub Actions RELEASE none chore USE IT FOR Maintenance, no src/test change EXAMPLE chore: update .gitignore for IDE files RELEASE none revert USE IT FOR Undo an earlier commit EXAMPLE revert: feat(order-service): add order cancellation RELEASE per rules hotfix TEAM USE IT FOR Urgent prod fix EXAMPLE hotfix(auth): reject expired refresh tokens RELEASE PATCH* security TEAM USE IT FOR Vulnerability fix EXAMPLE security(gateway): validate JWT audience claim RELEASE PATCH* infra TEAM USE IT FOR K8s, Helm, Terraform EXAMPLE infra(helm): raise order-service memory limit RELEASE none

The release column shows semantic-release defaults: breaking change gives MAJOR, feat gives MINOR, fix and perf give PATCH. *Custom types need a releaseRules entry and a commitlint type- enum entry (see Automation below). Commit message structure Header (required), body, footers: feat(order-service)!: replace REST callback with Kafka event Order confirmation now publishes OrderConfirmedEvent to the orders.confirmed topic instead of calling the billing webhook. BREAKING CHANGE: billing-service must consume orders.confirmed. Refs: PAY-142 Imperative, lowercase description, no trailing period. Short header: aim for 72 characters (commitlint limit: 100). Scope is the service, module or layer, in kebabcase. Body explains why, after a blank line. ! or a BREAKING CHANGE: footer means MAJOR. One logical change per commit; ticket in a footer.

Common scopes: order-service , payment-service , auth , api , kafka , db , config , helm , deps . ✗ B A D fixed stuff fix(payment-service): reject duplicate idempotency keys GOOD ✗ B A D Update OrderService.java refactor(order-service): extract PricingCalculator GOOD ✗ B A D feat: Added Kafka retry. feat(order-service): add Kafka retry with backoff GOOD GitHub labels Use group: value , lowercase, one label per group. Labels are not commit types. Labels classify the work item ( type: feature , type: bug ); commit types describe the code change ( feat , fix ). GitHub defaults Created with every new repo; plain names STD bug , documentation , duplicate , enhancement , good first issue , help wanted , invalid , question , wontfix Type type: <kind> , what the work item is type: bug , type: feature , type: enhancement , type: chore , type: security Priority priority: <level> , urgency, one per issue priority: critical , high , medium , low Component component: <service> , what is affected component: order-service , payment-service , kafka , database , helm , ci Environment env: <name> , where it occurs env: dev , env: staging , env: prod Review status status: <state> , where the PR stands status: needs-review , changes-requested , approved , blocked , ready-to-merge

Branch naming feature/ USE FOR New capability F LOW main → PR → main EXAMPLE feature/PAY-142-kafka-retry-backoff bugfix/ USE FOR Non-urgent bug F LOW main → PR → main EXAMPLE bugfix/ORD-87-null-device-ip hotfix/ USE FOR Urgent prod fix (PATCH) F LOW release tag → PR → main, then tag EXAMPLE hotfix/1.4.1-expired-token-fix refactor/ USE FOR Restructure only F LOW main → PR → main EXAMPLE refactor/BKP-31-extract-backup-validator

release/ USE FOR Stabilise a version F LOW main → fixes only → main, then tag EXAMPLE release/1.5.0 Lowercase, hyphens, ticket first, no spaces (Git also rejects ~ ^ : ? * in ref names). Delete branches after merge. GitFlow teams use develop in place of main for feature and bugfix work, and merge release and hotfix branches into both. Prefixes are a TEAM convention. Branches are temporary; tags are permanent. A hotfix branches from the released tag ( v1.4.0 ), ships as v1.4.1 , and merges back to main . A release branch takes version bump and fixes only, then ships as v1.5.0 . Pull request naming ✗ BAD TITLE Fix fix(payment-service): reject duplicate idempotency keys (PAY-142) GOOD TITLE

✗ BAD TITLE WIP kafka stuff feat(order-service): publish OrderConfirmed event GOOD TITLE (ORD-210) , opened as a Draft PR ✗ BAD TITLE Updated pom.xml build(deps): bump spring-boot to 3.4.0 GOOD TITLE ✗ BAD TITLE Hotfix for prod!! hotfix(auth): reject expired refresh tokens (SEC-31) GOOD TITLE ✗ BAD TITLE Release 1.5.0 chore(release): 1.5.0 GOOD TITLE With squash merge the PR title becomes the commit subject on main , so it must follow the commit format. One logical change per PR; use Closes #142 in the body to link issues. Git tags and Semantic Versioning MAJOR X.0.0 Breaking change: removed endpoint, incompatible event schema ( feat! / BREAKING CHANGE ) 2.0.0 MINOR 1.X.0 Backward-compatible new feature ( feat ) 1.5.0 PATCH 1.4.X Backward-compatible bug fix ( fix , perf , security ) 1.4.1 A bump resets the lower numbers to 0. Pre-release precedence, lowest to highest: 1.5.0-alpha.1 → 1.5.0-beta.1 → 1.5.0-rc.1 → 1.5.0 Release tag FORMAT vMAJOR.MINOR.PATCH v1.5.0 EXAMPLE N OT E The v is a tag convention, not part of SemVer Pre-release FORMAT -alpha.N , -beta.N , -rc.N EXAMPLE v1.5.0-rc.1 N OT E Sorts before the stable release Build metadata FORMAT +build 1.5.0+20261109 EXAMPLE N OT E Ignored when comparing versions Maven development FORMAT -SNAPSHOT 1.5.0-SNAPSHOT EXAMPLE N OT E Maven convention; dropped at release Per-service (monorepo) FORMAT service-vX.Y.Z order-service-v1.5.0 TEAM EXAMPLE N OT E One tag per deployable Docker / Helm FORMAT X.Y.Z (no v ) EXAMPLE acme/order-service:1.5.0 N OT E Helm appVersion: "1.5.0"

Create and push tags: # annotated tag: use for releases git tag -a v1.5.0 -m "Release 1.5.0" # pre-release git tag -a v1.5.0-rc.1 -m "Release candidate 1" # push one tag explicitly git push origin v1.5.0 # push commits + their annotated tags git push --follow-tags # list matching tags git tag -l "v1.5.*" # branch from a released tag git switch -c hotfix/1.5.1-fix-npe v1.5.0 # last resort: never reuse a published tag git tag -d v1.5.0 git push origin --delete v1.5.0 Automation and enforcement git commit → Husky commit-msg hook → commitlint lints message → GitHub Actions PR title + tests → semantic-release tag + release commitlint validates every commit message. npm i -D @commitlint/cli \ @commitlint/config-conventional // commitlint.config.js module.exports = { extends: ['@commitlint/config-conventional'], rules: { 'type-enum': [2, 'always', [ 'feat', 'fix', 'docs', 'style', 'refactor', 'perf', 'test', 'build', 'ci', 'chore', 'revert', 'hotfix', 'security', 'infra' ]] } }; Husky runs Git hooks on every commit (v9 syntax). In a Maven or Gradle repo, add a minimal package.json for tooling only. npm i -D husky npx husky init echo "npx --no -- commitlint --edit \$1" \ > .husky/commit-msg GitHub Actions blocks non-conforming PR titles. Pin to the current major version and check the action's releases. on: pull_request: types: [opened, edited, synchronize] jobs: pr-title: runs-on: ubuntu-latest steps: - uses: amannn/action-semantic-pull-request@v5 env: GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }} semantic-release derives version, tag and notes from commits. Defaults: breaking gives major, feat minor, fix and perf patch. Update the Maven or Gradle version in a build step. { "branches": ["main"], "plugins": [ ["@semantic-release/commit-analyzer", { "releaseRules": [ { "type": "hotfix", "release": "patch" }, { "type": "security", "release": "patch" } ] }], "@semantic-release/release-notes-generator", "@semantic-release/github" ] } Remember. Never reuse a published tag. Fix forward with the next patch version.

CHAPTER 08 Git Cheat Sheet The whole of Chapter 7 on one screen. What changed in this commit? feat , fix , docs … How do we triage this item? type: , priority: , status: Where does the work happen? feature/ , bugfix/ , hotfix/ Which version did we ship? v1.5.0 Commit message Lowercase, no period, about 72 characters. Body explains why. Footer: BREAKING CHANGE: and Refs: PAY-142 .

Commit types feat , fix , perf trigger a release. docs , style , refactor , test , build , ci , chore , revert do not. hotfix , security , infra are TEAM types.
